speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with a psychiatric condition and a new onset movement disorder. To begin our evaluation, can you describe the specific psychiatric symptoms you have been experiencing, such as mood changes, anxiety, or hallucinations?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the normal thyroid and metabolic panels, the involuntary movements are likely medication-induced. Can you describe exactly what the movements look like—such as a shuffling gait, lip smacking, or repetitive tongue movements—and do they persist even when you are sitting or lying down?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Dystonia (specifically Akathisia) secondary to Risperidone use.
